📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that seconda vittoria consecutiva e terza nelle ultime quattro partite per l'Inter U23, che batte 2-1 la capolista Potenza e sale momentaneamente al terzo posto in classifica. Grandissima prestazione da parte dei ragazzi di Vecchi, che giocano a viso aperto contro la dominatrice del girone C di Serie C e conquistano un altro successo prestigioso, confermando la propria fama di "ammazza big" (dopo i trionfi contro Catania, Foggia, Crotone e Salernitana). I nerazzurri di Vecchi passano in vantaggio al 16' con un gran gol di Marello, ma pochi minuti dopo Selleri trova il pareggio. Nella ripresa gli ospiti hanno la chance di ribaltare il risultato con un calcio di rigore assegnato per fallo di mano di Fiordilino su tiro di Petrungaro, ma Melgrati para il tentativo dal dischetto di Castorani. Nel finale l'Inter trova la giocata decisiva con Agbonifo, che si inventa un sinistro dalla distanza e fa esplodere la panchina nerazzurra.

Reti: 16' Marello (I), 23' Selleri (P), 85' Agbonifo (I).

Recent findings suggest that INTER U23 (3-4-2-1): 1 Melgrati; 75 Bovio, 19 Prestia, 5 Tosto; 27 Aidoo (80' 10 Agbonifo), 7 Kaczmarski, 8 Fiordilino, 3 Marello; 30 Mosconi (80' 29 Mancuso), 6 Charlys; 11 Zuberek (64' 99 Fumagalli). A disposizione: 22 Taho, 95 Raimondi, 2 Avitabile, 4 Cerpelletti, 14 Bovo, 15 Stante, 24 Re Cecconi, 37 Sorino, 80 Garonetti, 86 Jakirovic. Allenatore: Stefano Vecchi.

POTENZA (4-3-3): 17 Cucchietti; 26 Kirwan, 6 Loiacono (C), 47 Bura, 3 Russo (78' 98 Adjapong); 8 Castorani (68' 80 dos Santos), 24 Bando, 23 De Marco (78' 14 Franzolini); 30 Petrungaro, 70 Selleri (68' 9 Murano), 10 D'Auria (68' 77 Ghisolfi). A disposizione: 1 Franchi, 12 Gironi, 2 Verza, 7 Bruschi, 11 Mazzeo, 21 Manfredonia, 25 Staver. Allenatore: Ivan Tisci.

It has been revealed that arbitro: Riccardo Tropiano (sez. Bari).

Assistenti: Romagnoli - De Luca.

Ammoniti: Aidoo (I), Zuberek (I), Bura (P), Kaczmarski (I), Agbonifo (I).

'Am I supposed to answer that?': Erling Haaland breaks silence and distances himself from Man City cheating verdict as star striker insists 'I don't really know much... I was playing for Bryne Under 9s'

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.
  • Recent findings suggest that man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.

Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.

Recent findings suggest that man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Haaland was quizzed about the club's situation by Norwegian broadcaster TV2, after scoring in the national team's 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday.

The Man City star's initial answer lasted for two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges.

It has been revealed that erling Haaland insisted it was difficult for him to answer a question about Man City's guilty verdict, with the club appealing against the decision of an independent commission. Source: TV2Sport.

Haaland stressed he remains happy at the club after being asked about his future given the potential ramificiations if Man City fail with their appeal to overturn the verdict.

'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland began.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

Haaland continued by listing fellow Norwegians who had been at Man City at the time, joking that they may be in a better place to offer insight.

'There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think,' Haaland stated.

Industry observers note that 'Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can't remember.

The forward distanced himself from the case as he listed team he played from 2009-18, the time covered by the charges. Pictured: Haaland in action for Molde in 2018.

'But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

According to recent reports, 'A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a newly introduced nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that notes everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there.'.

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Haaland, who has won eight major honours at the club including the Treble in 2023, was asked about whether the case has affected his thoughts on his Man City future.

'I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,' Haaland responded.

In a recent development, 'I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

'I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're top of our group in Europe.

'Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.'.

Man City have won twice and lost three times in the Premier League since the independent commission verdict was declared in September.

Enzo Maresca's side have slipped to six points behind reigning champions Arsenal following their drop off in form.

Abbiamo vissuto tantissime esperienze entusiasmanti, dall’era Spalletti fino a Conte. La più grande è stata osservare la squadra capace di conquistare costantemente traguardi prestigiosi e di mantenersi sempre ad altissimi livelli”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli FcInter1908 come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Recent findings suggest that stefano Vecchi, tecnico dell'Inter U23, ha parlato in sala stampa dopo il successo contro il Potenza: "Oggi per vincere abbiamo avuto bisogno di tutti. Questa è la vittoria del gruppo, di tutti: del portiere che ha fatto parate importanti, degli attaccanti, di chi è entrato e ha risolto la partita come Agbonifo. Come ho sempre detto è un gruppo di ragazzi che lavora sodo e bene, si fanno sempre trovare pronti, e contro un Potenza di questo tipo ce n'era bisogno. Quando si gioca tutti al massimo delle potenzialità, quest'anno siamo competitivi e stiamo bene in campo con tutti. Poi è anche vero che nel secondo tempo il Potenza ci ha messo grande pressione. Siamo stati bravi anche a soffrire, cosa non scontata per una squadra della nostra età".

Si può dire che quest'anno la squadra ha compiuto il passo in avanti dal punto di vista della maturità?

Recent findings suggest that "Siamo cresciuti tutti, in un girone molto impegnativo e complicato come il C. Ci rendiamo conto di essere competitivi con tutti: l'anno scorso c'erano partite che per mezz'ora o dei tempi sembrava di essere in balia dell'avversario e di prendere delle imbarcate clamorose. Quest'anno invece no, un po' perchè la qualità dei ragazzi è alta, un po' perchè chi è rimasto ha un'esperienza diversa".

A inizio stagione forse una vittoria del genere non sarebbe arrivata: cosa è cambiato?

In a recent development, "Cambiato non lo so, sicuramente siamo una squadra che deve lavorare per migliorare. I ragazzi sono molto giovani, ma al tempo stesso non darei per scontata questa cosa: dobbiamo tenere i piedi per terra e continuare a lavorare sodo. Tanti dei nostri sono all'inizio della nostra carriera, non possono accontentarsi di una partita fatta bena all'interno di un campionato o di essere come adesso se vogliono giocare in Serie A, come giustamente ambiscono i nostri ragazzi".

Quanto aiutano partite come queste a crescere?

Industry observers note that "Sicuramente aiuta, a patto che si riesca a rimanere con i piedi per terra e non ci si senta arrivati dopo aver battuto la prima. La classifica parla chiaro, il Potenza non ha quei punti per caso e l'ha dimostrato anche oggi nel secondo tempo. Noi siamo stati in partita, quando ci siamo tutti e giochiamo da squadra possiamo vincere".

Charlys e Kaczmarski hanno disputato una buona gara.

It has been revealed that "Sono ragazzi con potenzialità importanti, sono i nostri giovani "più vecchi" essendo dei 2004, hanno già avuto esperienza e stanno dimostrando di essere pronti per un salto importante. Se sono qua è perchè prima non hanno dimostrato queste potenzialità, adesso le stanno tirando fuori e anche loro devono usare questa squadra come un trampolino di lancio, ma lo fai se la squadra raggiunge risultati: prima il gruppo e poi singolarmente arriveranno soddisfazioni".

Il Potenza ha la possibilità di rimanere al vertice?

"Ho visto un Potenza che ha provato vincere, consapevole della propria forza, e nel secondo tempo siamo stati un po' in affanno. Poi siamo stati bravi a portarla dalla nostra parte con la bravura di Melgrati e anche per quello che abbiamo creato. Il Potenza ha dimostrato di essere meritatamente là davanti, poi se riuscirà a rimanere là dipende dalla sua bravura e magari da qualche passo falso di qualche squadra importante. Ho vinto un campionato con la Feralpi Salò, è possibile tutto nel calcio, anche che qualche realtà che parte dietro possa superare le favorite".

Industry observers note that si aspettava un Potenza arrembante? Avevate preparato la partita così?

It has been revealed that "Il Potenza ha grandissima qualità, giocatori che sanno ribaltare l'azione con grande gamba e velocità. Sapevamo di questa loro qualità, ma non sempre si riesce a fare quello che si vorrebbe. Nel secondo tempo siamo costretti ad abbassarci perchè il Potenza ha spinto. Spesso gli episodi indirizzano la gara, oggi sono stati dalla nostra parte. credo comunque che la vittoria sia stata meritata. Abbiamo un portiere e lo paghiamo per parare! E poi, nella fatica, i miai ragazzo non hanno mai mollato: ci portiamo a casa anche quella convinzione di averla meritata".

Come mai c'è stata un'Inter diversa tra primo e secondo tempo?

Industry observers note that "Merito del Potenza. Noi siamo calati fisicamente con qualche ragazzo. Abbiamo avuto una settimana di stop, qualche ragazzo è andato via con le Nazionali, qualcuno è stato in Prima Squadra, qualcuno ha giocato tre partite in una settimana in Nazionale e altri che non hanno proprio giocato. Quelli che si sono allenati con noi erano in 7-8: quando c'è la sosta per le Nazionali per noi è un problema preparare fisicamente la squadra. Oggi abbiamo sofferto la veemenza del Potenza, forse avrei potuto fare qualche cambio prima per dare più freschezza".

Aurelio De Laurentiis, presidente del Napoli, è stato tra i protagonisti della prima edizione del premio “Eccellenza Calcistica Italiana”, manifestazione dedicata alle personalità che si sono distinte nel panorama calcistico nazionale. L’evento si è svolto a Villa Campolieto, a Ercolano, dove il patron azzurro ha ricevuto un riconoscimento nella categoria Fair Play, che vedeva tra i finalisti anche Andrea Belotti e Luca Percassi. Nel corso del suo intervento, De Laurentiis ha parlato anche del film dedicato al Centenario del Napoli: “La sceneggiatura del film del centenario la scrive il qui presente Maurizio de Giovanni. Il calcio in Inghilterra è nato con gli aristocratici. Non era un fatto popolare. Arrivarono a Napoli e iniziarono a giocare con gli scugnizzi. Il 1922 sembrerebbe la vera data, poi procrastinata al 1926 per la nascita del Napoli. Che non si chiama Società Sportiva, ma Calcio Napoli. Questo film è venuto talmente bene che una piattaforma importante come Amazon lo porterà nel mondo. Quando abbiamo vinto lo Scudetto con Conte, ho fatto un film e sono andato a Los Angeles: presi questo cinema e ho fatto questa anteprima dove sono arrivati questi tifosi dall’America. C’erano donne emozionatissime che dicevano di non capire nulla di calcio ma che si sono comunque fatte trascinare. Ho scoperto che a San Pedro ci sono 30mila tifosi del Napoli legati all’isola d’Ischia”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026.

Spending time in the company of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage demonstrates at grand venues like London Palladium.

On this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling. Yes, you read that right, Mr Warnock is here to launch his own pair of socks with a tipple of Famous Grouse whisky in hand.

The complements on Warnock's 77-year-old feet are soon over, though, and we can get on to talking about a life in football that started six decades ago as a winger for Chesterfield and has traversed 10 clubs as a player, 17 as a manager and more than 2,000 games in the dugout.

According to recent reports, so where to start? Maybe his reflections on nearly five decades in management – and how the whole conversation about feet is not too out of place….

Recent findings suggest that 'You don't realise how long it has been really, I started off just a team of ragamuffins as I call them,' he says in his iconic Yorkshire accent. 'They used to train on the green where I had digs in Hartlepool and asked me to coach them.

'I remember we scored from a set-piece we worked on, I was running up and down the touchline high-fiving everyone. I got the bug. I knew I could never get to the top as a player, I was quick but I was brainless.

Daily Mail Sport caught up with Neil Warnock to discuss his six decades in football.

After representing 10 different clubs as a player, Warnock became one of the most compelling managers in the game.

'I could've been a chiropodist if not in football. That could be on a quiz, couldn't it? I had bad feet at Scunthorpe, I used to get massive blisters so the physio there started getting me to do some of the players' feet.

In a recent development, 'I enjoyed doing ingrown toenails and things like that! So I thought why not? Then I had a practice in Sheffield. I had to make a decision when we won the league at Scarborough whether to go full-time or pack it in. I thought, "Oh, go on then, let's give it a little go".

'It's not worked out badly, really, has it?

Recent findings suggest that 'People come up to me every day and say, "You're a legend, you". And I say, "Oh, thank you very much". Then they tell me what club they support, I have had so many haven't I? Last week I went out for a minute and had four selfies. They all appreciate what I did for their club.

Recent findings suggest that 'There aren't as many characters in the game now, you wouldn't get upset with managers now like in my day because now they are that b****y boring! Some of them barely speak.

It has been revealed that 'They won't get the rapport we had. I managed at a good time. The way I managed, I needed that humour. I needed the lads to enjoy it. I signed a lot of players that many managers wouldn't touch with a barge pole, are you with me? They ended up getting me promotions.'.

The aforementioned humour brings us on to a private conversation he had with the great Pep Guardiola, one of the millions of anecdotes up Warnock's sleeve but one that he has not told until now.

In a recent development, 'I went to a training session and he asked me to say a few words,' explains Warnock. 'I said, "Well lads I bet you're glad I'm not your manager because we'd be kicking balls from there to there, chasing it, heading it, practicing our tackles"... everyone laughed.

Warnock views Pep Guardiola as the best manager of his lifetime, while the Spaniard praised the veteran's humour after once addressing his Man City squad at a training session.

Warnock has led teams to promotions on eight occasions over the course of his career.

Industry observers note that 'After the session we had a coffee and Pep remarked to me, "Neil, that was amazing, you know when you talked to the players? I understood why you had so many promotions".

In a recent development, 'He started counting and noted, "What we have is all these staff… computers, details, nutritionist, all these staff, but you know what we don't have? Humour". He noticed why my lads had done well in my teams, just in that meeting. It was good, that. He is amazing.

'Pep is the best manager of my lifetime. They say he had all the best players but it is not easy managing them. Pep did things with players and now there are non-league teams trying to play like Manchester City!'.

Warnock is now doing stage tours - Guardiola attended one last season - and had a tear in his eye when he stepped out at London Palladium given he used to watch demonstrates there with his mother, who was in a wheelchair, on the TV as a child.

Recent findings suggest that so what is Warnock up to these days? His current role is advisor at Torquay United but last management job was at Aberdeen two years ago… so is he out of the rat race for good this time?

Industry observers note that 'No, not really, no,' he says. 'I only work from February to April! So the phone will be on after Christmas. You never know, do ya? There will be someone thinking "why don't we get that Warnock in?".

According to recent reports, 'I've retired 40 times! Every time I have said it, I have meant it. But it's that dressing room camaraderie. There's something about football, when I look at some of the managers now… they just don't excite me.

Sources indicate that 'I remember Ruben Amorim (breaks down laughing). He's got his computer out on the bench! I remember watching and thinking, "I'm sorry, son, you need more than a computer to help you tonight!".

Warnock is currently doing stage tours, with Guardiola among the attendees last season.

Warnock's current role is advisor at Torquay United and briefly served as interim manager last season, with the 77-year-old admitting he had not completely ruled out a return to the dugout.

According to recent reports, 'And likewise, I see them making notes on the bench, oh my god. I think "what are you doing, your shopping list for Tescos?".

'I do enjoy walking and I enjoy photography, believe it or not. I go up the river with my phone, there's so many lovely things to see.

Industry observers note that 'I've got an electric bike and I sometimes do about 25 miles. I was thinking of doing a cycle of all my clubs but that would take me five years! They go at about 30mph down the hills, you've got to be careful, you wouldn't want to come off them.'.

He is also enjoying fishing, being with the family and playing golf with his son, a PGA rising star William - though Warnock Sr insists he often embarrasses himself playing off 'the ladies' tee'.

The thing that makes Warnock most proud is the four promotions at Wembley but also the togetherness he fostered in his many teams.

Industry observers note that he tells us: 'What I like about the teams I had, they all have reunions. You look at the tele now, someone will score a goal and kiss the badge… they won't have a reunion.

'When I go to these reunions, I see all my lads and how I blended that dressing room together and I look at the comradeship they still have now, they are the same as they were just a lot older.

Industry observers note that 'This year, my Scarborough team are having a 40-year celebration and the lads have invited me. I said there's no way I'm going out with that lot after the do because they can drink, let me tell you!'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

In a recent development, the chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his latest club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

According to recent reports, morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

Sources indicate that instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

According to recent reports, as for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

It has been revealed that arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be remarked that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a major summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

Sources indicate that “Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

It has been revealed that arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

According to recent reports, for the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

Industry observers note that chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

In a recent development, “After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0.

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr.

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”.

In a recent development, “It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We revealed our quality today. The result reflected that.”.

On his relationship with Kai Havertz:.

Sources indicate that “He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”.

Sources indicate that “We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”.

They were 1-0 down inside the opening two minutes but goals from Havertz and Odegaard have led them to victory. Chelsea suffer their first competitive defeat under Xabi Alonso.

Pedro’s cross from the right has too much on it and Chavarria cannot head it back across goal. Chelsea’s last chance might have been that Estevao effort which was brilliantly saved by Raya.

Madueke is brought on late for Saka.

There will be four added minutes.

Recent findings suggest that that is a stunning save from Raya that may have preserved Arsenal’s victory. Estevao cuts in from the right and curls one towards the top corner. It looks set for the net but somehow Raya makes a fantastic save to deny Estevao.

In a recent development, chelsea are bringing on Welbeck for Rogers, who is jeered by the Arsenal fans. Welbeck comes on with a note, that he gives to his captain James.

It has been revealed that arsenal have lost a bit of their composure and structure. I suspect that’s why Arteta has turned to Mikel Merino. He screamed at his bench immediately after a messy passage of play, and Merino emerged about 20 seconds later. Merino is very much the “sensible adult” sort of player, who should calm things down. Although he hasn’t yet.

England team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a big club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...

It has kicked off. Rogers is cynically tripped by Rice but the referee somehow does not see it. Rogers is incensed and marches over to Rice, who has massively got away with one there. "He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

Double change for Arsenal as Gyokeres and Merino come on for Havertz and Odegaard.

Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Recent findings suggest that that’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

Industry observers note that for the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. He plays the ball inside towards Havertz, who is in space on the edge of the Chelsea box. It is really intelligent from Havertz, who dummies it to take away Fofana and allows the ball to run through to Odegaard, who takes one touch before firing past Martinez.

Industry observers note that arsenal just scored the same goal they scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield. Tzolis into Odegaard, low and fast.

It has been revealed that it is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”.

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

Sources indicate that “We are better equipped,” stated Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very crucial.”.

According to recent reports, asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very key to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

In a recent development, two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”.

It has been revealed that chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, significant and small.

Industry observers note that “We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of massive personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”.

In a recent development, cosa pensate di fare con Francesco Camarda? Ruben Amorim non ha cercato di dribblare la domanda e in conferenza stampa ha affrontato il tema che riguarda l'attaccante del Milan: "Anche io ero un giocatore giovane che voleva tutto molto velocemente, e penso che questo succeda con un ragazzo che ha davvero tanta voglia di giocare, il che è una buona cosa. Mi piace molto. Credo abbia bisogno di tempo per adattarsi a un livello diverso. Giocare per il Milan è davvero difficile. È difficile per un ragazzo che ha esperienza come Ramos, di cui parlavate prima, figuriamoci per Camarda. Quindi ha bisogno di tempo per crescere, per sentirsi ambientato nel club. Non so cosa succederà a gennaio. Deve restare concentrato su queste partite. Nel calcio tutto cambia in una settimana, figuriamoci da qui a gennaio. Quindi l'obiettivo è il prossimo allenamento, la prossima partita, e può succedere di tutto".

In a recent development, amorim poi si congratula con il ct dell'Italia Under 21: "Sono davvero soddisfatto di come è tornato, forse perché ha cambiato ambiente. Ho sentito che Baldini ha parlato con lui. Non so cosa abbia detto al ragazzo, ma è tornato più felice. Quindi sono davvero contento per questa chiacchierata con Baldini e sono molto felice per Camarda. Queste cose possono succedere ai ragazzi giovani in un grande club: deve solo concentrarsi sul prossimo allenamento, godersi la prossima partita e le cose andranno a posto. Capisco la domanda su gennaio, ma gennaio è ancora molto lontano. Concentriamoci sulla prossima partita".

Sources indicate that A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio è intervenuto Raffaele De Leonardis (sindaco di Qualiano): “Quali sono i progetti da affiancare al centro sportivo del Napoli? Dopo la firma ho già pensato a cosa fare attorno alla zona. Quella sarà una cittadella dello sport, perché affianco ai terreni dove sorgerà il centro sportivo c’è uno stadio, ci sono campi da tennis e abbiamo in animo un palazzetto dello sport e una piscina. Oggi c’è la parte più difficile, quella della burocrazia e infrastrutture. In poco tempo che mi rimane come sindaco mi metterò a disposizione. Quante volte è saltata la trattativa con il Napoli e perché? La prima volta è saltata per il prezzo d’acquisto. Il Presidente De Laurentiis doveva valutare l’investimento. I primi terreni con destinazione urbanistica si parlava di 100 euro a metro quadro. Non c’era bisogno della Zes. Servivano 20 milioni di euro. Non era nelle disponibilità e intenzioni della società. Perché poi bisognava costruire il centro. E comparando con il Viola Park, finanziato dal 20% del Coni, ci fu un primo stop. Successivamente, la Zes paventava di superare vincoli urbanistici, allora si è cominciato a parlare di terreni agricoli. E quindi si è riallacciato il rapporto perché c’erano terreni che rientravano nei desideri della SSC Napoli. C’è stata una visita, sotto la pioggia, il famoso 30 marzo dell’anno dello Scudetto. Il Presidente del Napoli mi invitò allo stadio Maradona, vidi Massimo Boldi, c’era Serena Brancale, c’era De Martino. Quanti vaffa mi sono preso dal Presidente? Abbastanza (sorride ndr). Nell’ultima riunione c’era Chiavelli, c’erano Testa, Discepolo, c’era anche Edo e lì ho capito che forse c’eravamo. Se De Laurentiis si è messo in auto per vedere le distanze dalle stazioni ai terreni? Sì, la prima volta che venne a visitare i terreni prima di Napoli-Milan fece questo percorso in auto. Il Presidente De Laurentiis chiedeva quanto distasse dalla stazione di Afragola, ed erano circa 20 minuti, dalla stazione di Ponte Riccio al centro sono 10 minuti a piedi e da Varcaturo o zone residenziali dei giocatori sono 8 minuti di auto e dallo stadio sono 20 minuti con la tangenziale. Dall’aeroporto ancora meno, 12-13 minuti. De Laurentiis percepiva che la posizione era buona. Fece però un passo indietro in merito alla storia dei rifiuti tossici, si era spaventato, ma non era vero.

It has been revealed that quanto mi hanno dato fastidio le fake news attorno a questo? No, sono il Sindaco di Qualiano, ne sento tante. Però penso che ci sono solo pensieri in negativo. Ma pensiamo anche in positivo. Tutte queste problematiche potrebbero nascere, magari con la Zes. Ma noi che ci guadagniamo? Niente! C’è uno strumento di legge, sono stati fatti i migliori investimenti, noi stiamo sperando che non venga approvato? De Laurentiis ha firmato un atto notarile, un preliminare condizionato e se arriva l’autorizzazione, si trasforma automaticamente in definitivo. Lui che se ne fa di un terreno agricolo!? La Zes ha sette linee guida. Una delle linee riguarda l’attività produttiva per quanto riguarda turismo e sport. Noi non ci opporremo, perché sarebbe da folli. Chiederemo le infrastrutture che dovranno essere realizzate e aiuteremo il Napoli a realizzarle. Noi stiamo rispettando la legge. Se il prof Discepolo presenta il progetto definitivo in 10-15 giorni e partono i 90 giorni della Zes, seguiremo il countdown. Sentivo parlare di un’autorizzazione preliminare per il muro di cinta, con autorizzazione dei proprietari. Se ci sarà un laghetto? Non so se è un vezzo, ma servirà per irrigare i campi. Sarà a mo’ di cisterna. Se ci saranno hotel? Ci saranno sicuramente le stanze per i giocatori. De Laurentiis tiene tanto alla cantera, penso che farà anche un convitto per i giovani”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.
  • After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026.

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE massive take-aways….

It would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain.

And what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

Sources indicate that we can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

Much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

Industry observers note that white's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back.

Sources indicate that ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel stated on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa showed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

According to recent reports, trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred.

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion.

Recent findings suggest that no goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

According to recent reports, his swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men.

Industry observers note that he won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

According to recent reports, that is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that SSC Napoli Training Center – Gli azzurri si sono allenati in vista della prossima gara di campionato, sabato alle 20:45 contro il Torino al Maradona. Il gruppo è stato impegnato in una seduta pomeridiana svolgendo attivazione e lavoro tecnico-tattico.

Tutti i calciatori sono rientrati dagli impegni con le nazionali.

Alex Meret, in seguito a un trauma subìto in allenamento, si è sottoposto a esami strumentali, presso il Pineta Grande Hospital, che hanno evidenziato una frattura della quinta vertebra lombare.

Il calciatore azzurro ha già iniziato l’iter riabilitativo.

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday after Brazil's last-16 World Cup exit is behind his slow start with Real Madrid this season.

And the winger says he felt 'overwhelmed' by the interest of clubs such as Arsenal  and insecurity around his contract renewal talks in Madrid.

He has scored one goal and provided three assists in 12 games this season, and amid the criticism, manager Jose Mourinho has even said he should have left this summer to go somewhere he is 'respected'.

According to recent reports, vini Jr said: 'I don’t think I prepared better after the World Cup because the impact of this tournament is very significant for all Brazilians. Losing so early was something we didn’t expect.

'So I took advantage of the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years. This may have affected my start to the season.

In a recent development, 'Also, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs interested last summer, I felt really overwhelmed, as did the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long.

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday is behind his slow start to the season (Instagram: vinijr).

The Real Madrid star spent plenty of time relaxing on yachts as he visited Brazil, Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai (Instagram: vinijr).

The 26-year-old got around via private jet and said that he wants to 'enjoy life' (Instagram: vinijr).

In a recent development, 'Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult. I believe only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to maintain it for so many years, achieving the same numbers.

'I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve. I try to understand more about football, about the day-to-day, but I'm 26 years old and I have to enjoy life a little too.

Recent findings suggest that 'Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals, as in all other seasons. I believe I am preparing, evolving, because, in the most decisive moment of the season, I am always there.'.

Vini Jr spent part of his summer break in his home city of Sao Goncalo, as well as visiting Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai.

His Instagram was full of pictures of him relaxing on yachts, speeding around on a private jet, and showing off his fashionable outfits.

Arsenal enquired about the Brazilian superstar and reports suggested they were willing to offer him a mammoth £18.5million per season - more than any player at the club.

His contract expires at the end of the season and the club's position is that he must lower his demands if they are to agree an extension. They would still be willing to make him their joint-highest earner alongside Kylian Mbappe.

Recent findings suggest that he has often been a target of racism in Spain - there have been more than 20 such cases of alleged abuse towards him since he joined from Flamengo in 2018. The situation has reduced him to tears before, but he has insisted on staying in La Liga so that he doesn't 'give the racists what they want'.

The winger - who has scored one goal and provided three assists this season - was a target for Arsenal and could leave Madrid in January.

The winger is right now serving a four-match ban for pulling Villarreal star Nathan Saliba's hair.

And Mourinho said last month: 'If I were in his shoes, I probably wouldn't be here. I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected, but out of loyalty to Real Madrid and love for the club, he stayed.

'He believes things can improve, and he still has that smile. Nothing and no one can take it away from him.

In a recent development, 'He's a fantastic guy, and it's easy to get along with him. I spend a few minutes alone with him every day.

'I value him immensely because he always manages to live and survive with a smile.'.

Vinicius has been a phenomenon at Real Madrid, scoring 129 times in 388 games from the wing.

But the balance of power shifted to Mbappe when he joined from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 and talk of his future has increased.

There is a chance that, if Madrid go a third season in a row without significant silverware, they choose to rebuild and go in a different direction.

Moving away from the heavy 'superstar' model has worked for PSG and rewarded them with two Champions League titles in a row.

Vinicius had a tricky summer, being knocked out of the last 16 of the World Cup with Brazil and then missing his pre-season return date as his representatives tried to revive talks over a contract extension.

If an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling in January, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer for the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 08:03 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:49 EST, 16 November 2026.

Romelu Lukaku has revealed his retirement from international football in a 'bombshell' decision that has left the Belgian press utterly stunned.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward, 33, vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team, although he now appears to have changed his mind over his future.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku took to social media on Monday morning to break the unexpected news.

It has been revealed that '16 years old,' his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Sources indicate that 'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

It has been revealed that 'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

Belgium legend Romelu Lukaku has revealed his decision to retire from international football.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking on the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retires as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

Belgian newspapers were caught out by the shock announcement, which was described as an 'unexpected bombshell' by outlet HLN on Monday.

Lukaku's stock within the international set-up has fallen since he promised the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament in January.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the tournament under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

Axel Witsel sent a heartfelt message to Lukaku on Instagram: 'Thanks for everything, legend'.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute - and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

According to recent reports, 'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

In a recent development, 'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'.

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that 'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

Sources indicate that but here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

Recent findings suggest that "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

Recent findings suggest that “Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Recent findings suggest that benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

In a recent development, united should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

It has been revealed that yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

Sources indicate that “We’re bitterly disappointed,” remarked Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

Sources indicate that but clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

Industry observers note that how had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their fresh sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

In a recent development, it could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Recent findings suggest that speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

Recent findings suggest that david Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having mentioned that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Industry observers note that shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Altra vittoria della Lazio, altro gol per Davide Frattesi, che ora è a quota cinque reti in campionato.
  • Queste le parole sull'obbiettivo della Lazio: "Vogliamo arrivare a 40 punti, poi chi vivrà vedrà.
  • Sula mentalità della squadra di Gattuso: "È figlia del pensiero del mister che dice che quando uno ha la testa sotto la sabbia bisogna schiacciarla più forte.

Altra vittoria della Lazio, altro gol per Davide Frattesi, che ora è a quota cinque reti in campionato. Al termine del match l'ex Inter ha parlato ai canali ufficiali del club: "Il gol? Ogni tanto in allenamento lo provo. Non avevo ancora fatto un gol e mi sono preso gli insulti del mister. Oggi non dico che ero sorpreso, ma è uscita veramente una bella cosa. Continuerò a provarci durante la settimana e prenderò ancora gli insulti del mister", le sue parole riportate da Lalaziosiamonoi.it.

Queste le parole sull'obbiettivo della Lazio: "Vogliamo arrivare a 40 punti, poi chi vivrà vedrà. Era l’obbiettivo che avevamo e continuiamo ad avere. Non abbiamo lo status per poter dire che vogliamo arrivare in Conference, Europa o Champions. Dobbiamo vivere alla settimana e tutto ciò che verrà dopo sarà guadagnato".

Sula mentalità della squadra di Gattuso: "È figlia del pensiero del mister che dice che quando uno ha la testa sotto la sabbia bisogna schiacciarla più forte. Certe partite non sai mai come girano, come quella contro il Milan. Questo è figlio di quel pensiero e dell’atteggiamento del gruppo, che è sano e fatto di ragazzi che quando vanno in campo sono cattivi.”.

E ha concluso: "Facciamo una settimana di lavoro molto intensa. Quando gli altri finiscono la benzina noi abbiamo ancora qualcosa nel serbatoio. Facendo una gara a settimana è anche più facile gestire i carichi. Questa è la strada e se non vai forte fai fatica. Questa deve essere la base, poi qualsiasi cosa si può migliorare. L’attitudine al lavoro o ce l’hai o non ce l’hai”.

81′ Ammonito Raffaelli per un fallo su Zappalà.

78′ Doppio cambio Napoli: escono Favicchio e Barido ed entrano Natale e Rovetini.

77′ Napoli in dieci! Espulso Marotta per doppia ammonizione: l’azzurirno ha fermato una ripartenza di Ciani.

Sources indicate that 75′ Perugia pericoloso! Imbuacata di Bellali per Agnissan ma, dopo una serie di rimpalli, il Napoli riesce a liberare.

72′ Altra palla recuperata del Napoli, Barido intercetta e serve Favicchio: pallone leggermente lungo che non permette all’azzurrino di controllare nell’area di rigore aversaria.

69′ Pressing alto del Napoli, Liccardo ruba palle dentro l’area di rigore umbra ma, invece di tirare, serve Mane e gli ospiti si rifugiano in corner.

66′ Barido per Esposito, che viene atterrato al limite di rigore umbra ma l’arbitro fa continuare. Qualche protesta da parte degli azzurrini.

Recent findings suggest that 63′ Napoli pericoloso! Tiro di Esposito dal limite dell’area di sinistro: Strappini si allunga e salva all’altezza dell’incrocio dei pali, corner per i partenopei.

59′ Grande occasione per il Napoli! Lancio in profondità per Mane che, a tu per tu con il portiera, tira troppo debolmente, facilitando così l’intervento di Strappini.

57′ Doppio cambio nel Napoli: Mane per Saviano e D’Angelo per De Stefano.

57′ Ammonito Marotta per aver fermato una ripartenza di Ciani.

55′ Gol del Perugia! Palla tra linee per Perugini, che controlla di sinistro e tira di destro e pallone che si insacca all’angolino.

54′ Doppio cambio nel Perugia: Vanni e Mercio fanno spazio a Raffaelli e Agnissan.

47′ C’è stao un cambio anche nel Perugia: Bellali è entrao al posto di Pierangelini.

47′ Tiro-cross dalla sinistra di Mercio: palla che finisce fuori sul secondo palo.

46’Grande occasione per il Napoli! Favicchio per Saviano sulla sinistra, sponda di Saviano per Barido che entra in area e calcia sopra la traversa.

Cambio nel Napoli: esce Melynk ed entra Liccardo.

44′ Barido prova a sorprendere Strappini con una punizione beffarda, l’estremo difensore riesce a rientrare e a far suo il pallone.

42′ Favicchio premia la progressione di Santella sulla sinistra, traversone al centro bloccato da Strappini.

36′ Conclusione dalla distanza di sinistro da parre di Melnyk: sfera che si spegne sul fondo.

31′ Ammonito Malfatti per un brutto fallo su Zappalà.

28′ Grande occasione per il Perugia! Palla dalla sinistra raccolta da Vanni in piena area di rigore partenopea, che controlla e conclude di sinistro: pallone a lato.

27′ Il Napoli reclama un rigore per una trattenuta (non pesantissima, ma c’è), di Di Salvatore su Melnyk: l’arbitro ha fatto continuare.

It has been revealed that 23′ Occasione Napoli! Favicchio serve sulla corsia sinistra Baridò, che conclude in porta: Cesarini devia. L’azzurrino poteva sia servire Esposito che concludere in maniera più incisiva.

In a recent development, 19′ Calcio di punizione di Perugini respinto dalla barriera, pallone che, per poco, non diventa buono l’inserimento sul secondo palo di Pierangelini. Corner per gli ospiti.

18′ Ammonito Vanni per un brutto fallo su Chiummariello, partito in ripartenza.

Industry observers note that 17′ Doppia grande occasione per il Perugia! Corner corto di Di Salvatore: traversone che pesca Merci, il cui tiro viene deviato e sfiora l’incrocio dei pali. Sull’angolo successivo stacca Peruzzi, ma è bravissimo Saviano a deviare nei pressi della linea di porta.

It has been revealed that 11′ GOOL NAPOLI! Ottima sponda di Saviano per Favicchio, che si accentra e beffa Strappini con una conclusione di destro che si insacca nell’angolino.

9′ Imbucata per Cianni, che prova a mettere il pallone in mezzo: bravissimo Merone a leggere la giocata e a bloccare in uscita il pallone.

6′ Perugia pericoloso! Cross al centro per Pierangelini che, in area di rigore partenopea, colpisce il pallone con la spalla e non di testa: sfera che si spegne sul fondo.

3′ Santella si propone sulla sinistra e realizza un traversone al centro che, però, viene bloccato da Strappini.

Napoli (4-2-3-1): 1 Merone, 2 Melnyk, 3 Santella, 4 De Stefano, 5  Zappalà, 6 Marotta, 7  Esposito , 8 Chiummariello, 9 Saviano, 10 Barido, 11 Favicchio A disposizione 12 Capasso, 13 Candela, 14 Natale, 15 Liccardo, 16 D’Angelo, 17 Pepe, 18 Anic, 19 Mane, 20 Rovetini 21 Riccio All.Antonio Nocerino.

According to recent reports, perugia (4-3-3): 1 Strappini, 2 Giambarveri, 3 Di Salvatore, 4 Malfatti, 5 Peruzzi, 6 Cesarini, 7 Pierangelini, 8 Perugini, 9 Vanni,, 10 Mercio, 11 Ciani. Benvenuti alla diretta testuale di IamNaples.it di Napoli-Perugia, gara valida per la nona giornata del campionato Primavera 2 girone B. Gli azzurrini sono decimi, a cinque punti dalla zona play-off, proprio il Bari occupa l’ultima posizione utile per andare oltre la regular season. Il primo posto vale la promozione diretta, in questo momento lo occupa il Catanzaro che ha dieci punti in più degli azzurrini. A Cercola arriva il Perugia che è terzo in classifica con diciotto punti, otto in più del Napoli. La squadra di Nocerino in campionato è reduce da due pareggi a reti bianche contro Monopoli e Frosinone mentre il Perugia, dopo la sconfitta di Benevento, prima della sosta ha battuto 3-2 il Pescara.

Scegli FcInter1908 come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Mattia Marello, esterno sinistro dell'Inter U23 e autore del primo gol nella vittoria contro il Potenza, ha parlato in conferenza stampa al termine del match: "Sono super contento per la squadra e per il mio gol perché ha contribuito alla vittoria. Sono molto contento della prestazione perché era una gara difficile, contro una squadra che arrivava da un periodo importante, che è a +9 sulla seconda".

Recent findings suggest that cosa scatta nella testa di ragazzi come te alla prima esperienza tra i professionisti quando si è chiamati ad affrontare squadre di categoria? Cosa vi viene chiesto?

"Venivamo da una settimana difficile, io come tanti altri siamo stati in Nazionale, altri erano con la Prima Squadra, e quindi non siamo riusciti ad allenarci bene. Abbiamo preparato la partita in pochi giorni, ma sono stati molto importanti perché abbiamo fatto gruppo. Il mister ci ha parlato tanto prima e dopo l'allenamento, ci ha detto molto del Potenza insieme al suo staff e l'abbiamo preparata alla grande. Eravamo gasati".

Difficile preparare una gara con l'uscita di GTA?

"GTA? Non ho la Play Station, non è un mio problema... Magari altri hanno sofferto questo momento, ma non è il mio caso! Sono molto contento per la partita, eravamo gasati anche prima, il mister ci ha fatto un bel discorso e ci ha preparati. Sapevamo che non sarebbe stata una partita come le altre".

In cosa puoi migliorare ancora?

"Parlo sempre tanto con il mister e i suoi collaboratori, lo chiedo anche io. Io cerco di migliorarmi ogni giorno su tutto, anche sulle cose in cui sono più forte, però principalmente cerco di allenare il piede debole e le letture difensive per diventare un calciatore completo".
